content: <thought>The NMR data show a para‑disubstituted benzene (four aromatic protons as two sets of 2 H) and an –CH₂‑CH₂‑ fragment giving two triplets (2 H each) at ~2.6 ppm and ~2.8 ppm. The 13C spectrum has eight signals: six aromatic carbons and two aliphatic carbons (≈43 ppm for the benzylic CH₂ and ≈39 ppm for the CH₂ attached to a chlorine). This fits a para‑chloro‑substituted benzene bearing a 2‑chloroethyl group (Cl‑CH₂‑CH₂‑). The SMILES for this compound is **Clc1ccc(cc1)CCCl**.
